bib.title: TriviaQA: A Large Scale Distantly Supervised Challenge Dataset for Reading Comprehension
bib.venue: ACL 2017 (55th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics), pages 1601-1611

question: Can a reading-comprehension dataset built from trivia questions written independently of the evidence documents, with evidence gathered afterwards, be larger and harder than existing ones?
hypothesis: Decoupling question writing from evidence collection yields questions that are more compositional and need more lexical, syntactic and multi-sentence reasoning than SQuAD, so current models fall well short of humans.
contributions: Over 650K question-answer-evidence triples, with questions from trivia enthusiasts independent of the evidence documents
A manual analysis quantifying dataset quality and the challenges involved
Experiments with two baseline methods showing the tasks are not easily solved
A clean human-verified subset of 1975 question-document-answer triples

method.summary: Question-answer pairs are scraped from 14 trivia websites, then evidence is gathered afterwards from Bing web search (top 10 pages) and from Wikipedia pages for entities linked in the question with TAGME. Documents lacking the answer string are dropped, giving distant supervision. Baselines are a random-entity heuristic, a LambdaMART entity ranker and BiDAF with truncated documents.
method.task: reading comprehension / question answering with distantly supervised evidence documents

datasets.name: TriviaQA (Wikipedia domain)
datasets.split: random 80% train, 10% dev, 10% test of QA pairs
datasets.source: Questions from 14 trivia and quiz-league websites; evidence is Wikipedia pages for entities found with TAGME
datasets.preprocessing: Questions under four tokens removed. Evidence lacking the answer string removed. Documents for one question pooled (1.8 per question on average), evaluated per question.

datasets.name: TriviaQA (Web domain)
datasets.source: Top 10 crawled pages from the top 50 Bing Web search API URLs, query is the question (answer not used)
datasets.preprocessing: Trivia sites and URLs with trivia, question or answer removed; PDFs and ill-formatted documents pruned; each question-answer-document tuple is an independent data point; evaluated per document

datasets.name: TriviaQA verified subsets
datasets.size: Wiki: 297 dev / 584 test questions (305 / 592 documents). Web: 322 dev / 733 test questions (325 / 769 documents)
datasets.source: Questions and documents a human annotator answered correctly
datasets.preprocessing: Annotator answered 986 (Wikipedia) and 1345 (Web) dev and test questions, abstaining if the minimal facts were absent

models.name: Random entity baseline
models.architecture: heuristic: pick a random entity of the question's Wikipedia pages that does not occur in the question

models.name: Entity classifier (LambdaMART)
models.architecture: boosted-tree ranker over candidate answers, RankLib implementation, context and Wikipedia-catalog features

other.candidates: n-grams (n in [1,5]) in sentences sharing at least one word with the question that are titles of Wikipedia articles

models.name: BiDAF (modified)
models.architecture: RNN at character, token and phrase level with question-context attention, outputs start and end positions

other.span_label: first match of the answer string in the document
other.multi_doc: predict per document, score(A_i) = sum_k c_{i,k}, take the highest

training.objective: BiDAF: answer start/end span prediction with spans approximated by the first answer string match; classifier: LambdaMART ranking with score(a+|q,D) > score(a-|q,D)
training.seq_len: 800 words at test; training uses only documents where the answer appears in the first 400 tokens

other.bidaf_wiki_train: not stated beyond the first-400-token filter

inference.decoding: BiDAF: highest summed-confidence candidate across documents
inference.retrieval: Evidence is given, not retrieved at test time (Bing top 10 pages or TAGME-linked Wikipedia pages)

metrics.name: Exact match (EM)
metrics.definition: As SQuAD; for Wikipedia-entity answers, Wikipedia aliases count as valid; otherwise one given answer

metrics.name: Oracle
metrics.definition: Upper bound on EM: answer found in the (truncated) evidence, or in the candidate set for the classifier

eval.protocol: Wikipedia scored per question, Web scored per document. Distant-supervision dev/test plus human-verified dev/test subsets. No significance tests.

availability.data: http://nlp.cs.washington.edu/triviaqa/ (also an unfiltered release of 110,495 QA pairs and 740K documents)

limits: Distant supervision is noisy: evidence contains the answer for only about 75% of questions, and the span is approximated by the first string match.

BiDAF could not read whole documents: truncated to 800 words, trained only on documents with the answer in the first 400 tokens, and Web training used a sample of 80,000 documents. Oracle is below 100% because of this.
Only three simple baselines, no tuning details, seeds or hyperparameters reported.
Authors leave abstention (documents without the answer), multi-instance learning, KB use and scalable use of all data to future work.

Dated: 2017 extractive-reader baselines. Later work (retrievers, LLMs) uses TriviaQA as open-domain or closed-book QA, which this paper does not evaluate; this paper offers the unfiltered release for that.
